sections.h2: Where is Everett and how large is it?
sections.html:
Everett is a small, dense city in Middlesex County directly north of Boston, bordering the Charlestown neighborhood. It covers only about 3.7 square miles and held 49,075 residents at the 2020 census.

That works out to roughly 14,364 people per square mile, so houses sit close together and lots are small. Everett borders Malden to the north, Revere to the east, Chelsea to the southeast, Medford and the Malden River to the west, and the Mystic River to the south. Most of the housing is on tight streets near Broadway, with industrial land along the water.

sections.h2: What is the history of Everett?
sections.html:
Everett was part of Charlestown and later Malden, and it separated from Malden in 1870. It was named for Edward Everett, a former governor and Harvard president, and it became a city in 1892.

Landfill has pushed the shoreline outward over the centuries, and at some point between 1905 and 1912 fill connected the mainland to what had been White Island in the Mystic River. A refinery opened by Beacon Oil in 1920 and closed in 1965, and the tank farm remained. Everett was also the last American city with a two-chamber legislature, until voters approved a new charter in November 2011 that created an eleven-member City Council.

Everett's economy is built on energy, a large casino resort, retail and food manufacturing. A few named employers and sites from the city's history:

  • Encore Boston Harbor, the Wynn resort that opened on June 23, 2019
  • The Mystic Generating Station, which Wikipedia describes as the largest-capacity electrical plant in the state
  • The Everett Marine Terminal, which began importing liquefied natural gas in 1971
  • Leavitt Corporation, which has made Teddie Peanut Butter in the city since 1924
  • Gateway Center off Route 16, a large retail district

Wynn Resorts called the project a 2.6 billion dollar development. Wikipedia also notes that people are seeking homes in Everett to live near downtown Boston while avoiding the higher living costs in Boston, Cambridge or Somerville.

Everett grew fast in its early decades, shrank for a while, and has been climbing again. The Census Bureau count rose 17.8 percent between 2010 and 2020, and the 2025 estimate is higher still.

sections.h2: What does the housing stock look like in Everett?
sections.html:
Everett had 18,208 housing units and 17,211 households in 2020, with 5.5 percent of units vacant. The census reported a homeowner vacancy rate of 0.9 percent and a rental vacancy rate of 4.0 percent.

With so little land, houses here tend to be compact. A seller with a tenant, a repair backlog or an inherited house still has more than one way to sell.

sections.h2: How do roads and transit shape selling in Everett?
sections.html:
Broadway, part of Route 99, is the main business street, and MBTA bus routes converge at Everett Square with a bus lane on Broadway from Glendale Square to Sweetser Circle. Route 16 crosses the southern part of the city and links to U.S. Route 1 and Interstate 93, which both run just outside the city limits.

The Orange Line stops at Wellington, just across the line in Medford, and the commuter rail stops in Chelsea. Buyers who commute into Boston value this, so a house within walking distance of the bus corridor can attract commuters. If your lot has off-street parking, say so in any listing or offer request.

sections.h2: What big projects are changing Everett?
sections.html:
Several large projects are reshaping the waterfront. Knowing about them helps a seller describe the area accurately.

  • In December 2023 the Conservation Law Foundation announced a settlement with Exxon over its tank site, which was sold for cleanup and redevelopment, starting with raising the land and adding apartment buildings near Route 16. Exxon also agreed to a deed restriction barring fossil fuel storage there.
  • Davis Companies completed a 72.5 million dollar purchase of nearly 100 acres of the former tank farm, according to a Boston Globe report cited by Wikipedia.
  • A 700 megawatt, four-hour battery received approval from the Energy Facilities Siting Board.
  • MassDOT is designing a bike and pedestrian bridge from the Encore harborwalk to Somerville's Draw Seven park.
  • The New England Revolution have plans for a soccer stadium in the city.

Construction can mean noise and truck traffic near the Mystic River for years. None of this changes what your own house is worth on a given day, and we do not predict prices, but it is useful context when a buyer asks what is going on nearby.

sections.h2: Is flooding a concern for an Everett house?
sections.html:
Everett is low-lying, with an average elevation of about 10 feet, and the city has a long waterfront on the Mystic River. When Exxon's former tank site was sold for redevelopment in late 2023, the plan included raising the land to avoid climate-related flooding, according to Wikipedia.

The lesson for a seller is practical. A buyer or lender may ask for the flood zone of your lot, and a basement that has taken on water will come up in an inspection. Check the zone and keep any repair or insurance records handy.

sections.h2: What does Massachusetts require when an Everett house sells?
sections.html:
The deed is subject to a state excise tax under chapter 64D of the General Laws, which applies when the price exceeds one hundred dollars, and it is figured on the price excluding any loan that stays on the property. Your closing attorney calculates it.

You also need a smoke and carbon monoxide certificate of compliance from the local fire department. The state Department of Fire Services says to call the department as soon as the closing date is set, and that a fee applies. If your alarms are old, replace them first.

Property tax bills are separate. The Appellate Tax Board guide says tax is generally due on August 1, November 1, February 1 and May 1 in towns that bill quarterly, and that the abatement deadline is tied to the first installment. Ask the Everett assessors which schedule the city uses.

sections.h2: Who runs Everett and where do the kids go to school?
sections.html:
Everett has a mayor-council government, and the mayor serves a four-year term. The city has ten public schools, including elementary schools, K to 8 schools and Everett High School, which moved to 100 Elm Street starting with the 2007 to 2008 school year.

Pope John XXIII High School, a Catholic high school, closed on May 31, 2019. For questions about permits, rental rules or code enforcement before a sale, contact City Hall directly, since we could not open an official city page to confirm specific local rules.

sections.h2: What are the ways to sell an Everett house?
sections.html:
The three usual routes are a listing, a sale by owner and a cash sale. A cash sale tends to appeal when time matters or the house needs work.

  • A listing can reach many buyers but involves showings and repair requests.
  • A sale by owner saves a fee but puts the work on you.
  • A cash buyer purchases as is and can close on a date you choose.

We buy houses in Everett as they are, including ones with tenants, liens or repair needs. Request an offer, compare it to your other options, and decide at your own pace.

faqs.q: How many people live in Everett, MA?
faqs.a: The 2020 census counted 49,075 residents on about 3.7 square miles. The Census Bureau estimate for July 2025 is 53,572.
Everett is in Middlesex County, directly north of Boston and next to the Charlestown neighborhood.

faqs.q: Do I need a smoke detector inspection to sell in Everett?
faqs.a: Yes. Massachusetts requires a certificate of compliance for smoke and carbon monoxide alarms from the local fire department when a home is sold. Call as soon as the closing date is set.

faqs.q: Who pays the deed excise tax on a Massachusetts sale?
faqs.a: The excise is imposed on the deed under chapter 64D of the General Laws and is based on the sale price. Who pays is normally set in the purchase contract, so ask your attorney how it will be handled.

faqs.q: Can I sell an Everett house that needs repairs?
faqs.a: Yes. You can sell it as is to a cash buyer, or fix it first and list it. Compare the repair cost and time with a cash offer.
